sentences.text:
3. Petitioners-accused and respondent No.2-complainant are physically present before the Court along with their respective counsel and they admit the contents of the Joint Memo dated 04.03.2026, which read as under:-
"JOINT MEMO

The petitioners and the Respondent No.2 in the above case submits as follows:
The Respondent No.2 submits that the Respondent No.2 filed the P.C.R. before the trial court for the offence under section 419, 420 & 506 of the I.P.C. against the petitioners and others and after investigation the Respondent police has filed the charge sheet against the Petitioners and others.
The Petitioners submits that at the intervention of the well- wishers the Respondent No.2 and the Petitioners settled the dispute among themselves.

WHEREFORE, the Petitioners and the Respondent No.2 submits that the charge sheet filed against the Petitioners who are the Accused No.1, 4, 5, 6, 14 & 16 discharge them from the offence under section 419, 420 & 506 of the I.P.C. in the interest of justice and equity."
4.

In view of the aforesaid settlement entered into between the petitioners and respondent No.2, I pass the following:
NC: 2026:KHC:13296 HC-KAR ORDER (i) The petition is disposed of in terms of the Joint Memo, dated 04.03.2026.
(ii) The proceedings in C.C.No.59961/2024 (arising out of PCR No.59946/2023)
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 504, 506 r/w.
Section 34 of IPC pending on the file of XI ACJM at Bengaluru, insofar as the petitioners-accused Nos.1, 4, 5, 6, 16 and 14 are concerned are hereby quashed.

Sd/-
(S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR) JUDGE BMC List No.: 2 Sl No.: 7 Mr. Syed Fayaz vs State Of Karnataka on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106225228/
